assessment.nobel_worthiness: A transformative empirical account of long-run inequality, wealth concentration and tax avoidance with major consequences for research and public understanding.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez and Zucman form a coherent core spanning historical distributional evidence, top-income measurement and offshore wealth.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda has been extensively developed, replicated and incorporated into central debates on growth, distribution and taxation.
uncertainties: The appropriate scope of credit extends beyond three researchers in several underlying data-building projects.
Interpretation of distributional series and policy implications remains actively contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work substantially changed understanding of how technology and trade reshape local labour demand, employment and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson provide a strongly connected body of influential evidence on task change and trade-shock exposure; Katz is also an important intellectual contributor.
assessment.maturity: Its methods and conclusions have generated a large literature and remain highly relevant to contemporary structural transformation.
uncertainties: Separating trade, automation and other coincident local shocks remains empirically demanding.
The discovery description combines several related rather than wholly singular contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data made intergenerational mobility measurable at unprecedented scale and recast debates about equality of opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are a clear core for the linked methodological and substantive programme; Katz is an important collaborator.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been widely studied across places and cohorts and have already reshaped empirical public economics.
uncertainties: Administrative-data coverage and cross-country generalizability vary.
The translation from measured mobility to causal policy prescriptions is incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evolutionary analysis of routines and organizational change offered a durable alternative framework for understanding innovation, firm behavior and economic dynamism.
assessment.attribution: Winter is indispensable to the contribution, though its intellectual development is closely associated with broader evolutionary-economics work.
assessment.maturity: The framework has had decades to influence organizational economics, innovation studies and empirical research on firms.
uncertainties: A single-recipient formulation may understate essential co-development of the research tradition.
The breadth of the framework makes a sharply delimited prize citation difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation programme provided a powerful quantitative framework for assessing how distorted resource allocation can account for large productivity and income gaps.
assessment.attribution: Klenow, Hsieh and Restuccia are central contributors to the principal theoretical and empirical formulations.
assessment.maturity: The approach has generated a large follow-on literature across countries, sectors and historical settings.
uncertainties: Measured wedges can reflect multiple mechanisms and are not always direct evidence of specific distortions.
Estimated aggregate gains depend materially on modeling and measurement choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The systematic long-run comparative history of crises, debt and default helped make financial fragility a central historical and macroeconomic research subject.
assessment.attribution: Reinhart and Rogoff are the identifiable joint authors of the core comparative synthesis.
assessment.maturity: The work has had enduring influence on scholarship and policy discussion across successive financial episodes.
uncertainties: Historical coding, comparability and quantitative claims require continual scrutiny.
Some prominent conclusions and their policy use have been disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The programme demonstrated that management practices and organizational capital are measurable, consequential sources of firm productivity and cross-country performance.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are central originators, with Sadun an important contributor to the broader empirical research programme.
assessment.maturity: Its survey, experimental and administrative-data applications have accumulated across firms and countries.
uncertainties: Management measurement may partly capture other firm attributes.
The relative roles of selection, complementarities and causal managerial change remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work established foundational economic ways to analyse exhaustible resources, natural capital and the intertemporal conditions for inclusive wealth.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are closely associated with foundational contributions to resource and environmental economics.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have had long influence and increasing relevance as biodiversity and sustainability measurement have become central economic concerns.
uncertainties: Valuing biodiversity and substitutability between natural and produced capital remains intrinsically difficult.
The broad contribution has several other major contributors whose credit would require careful delimitation.
